note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses) from the 15-17 Oct review round, recovered from the workflow transcripts after the device move. Not yet acted on.

item-quality.verdict: The item is mostly sound but should not be accepted unchanged: there is one medium oracle/spec mismatch and two low issues. What holds up: start.grc fails at V3 for the stated reason (Add Const out(0) and Low Pass Filter in(0) are not connected). The fault is a realistic deleted_connection with exactly one restoring edge. The level is right (L1: 5 functional blocks, single-rate) and so is the family (repair). The instruction states every number used by the frequency, DC and harmonic checks, names the observation point (shaped_sine.dat, float) and does not leak the fix. My own band-pass alternative (Band Pass Filter 800-1600 Hz, gain 0.7854, no Add Const) also passes V6, as do the three author variants. Main problem: the max_abs check (±5 %, tolerance not stated) is stricter than the stated '>= 99 % power below 2.4 kHz' limit. Solutions that meet every stated number (e.g. cutoff 3.3 kHz: band_fraction 0.997, rms 0.711) fail on max_abs 0.948, whether they are scaled to fundamental 1, peak 1 or RMS 0.707. Dropping max_abs keeps every gate passing (10/10 mutants still killed; verified on a scratch copy). Minor: a sine-source replacement that ignores the repair passes V6, and the p2p labels mean nothing when the start graph never runs. Scratch work is in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-08 and in the session scratchpad's rev08 folder; the task directory was not modified.

findings.claim: The max_abs check (expect 1.0, rel_tol 0.05) sets a tolerance the instruction never states. It is also stricter than the harmonic limit the instruction does state. The instruction makes 'at least 99 % of the output power below 2.4 kHz' the number that defines 'essentially none of the harmonics'. But up to 1 % harmonic power lets a linear-phase filtered square wave have a peak up to about 10 % below its fundamental amplitude. So a solution that meets every stated number (harmonic share >= 99 %, sine amplitude 1, RMS about 0.707) can still fail V6. In practice the oracle requires roughly >= 99.8 % in-band power, which is a hidden requirement.
findings.evidence: I ran the start graph with only the missing connection restored and the Low Pass Filter set to cutoff 3300 Hz, width 1000 Hz (Multiply Const 0.7854 kept). Ladder result: band_fraction 0.997059 PASS, rms 0.711424 PASS, mean 0.0 PASS, peak_freq 1200 PASS, max_abs 0.948435 FAIL, so first_failed is V6. With cutoff 3400 Hz and width 800 Hz: band_fraction 0.995278, rms 0.71017, max_abs 0.932001, which also fails V6. None of the natural ways to scale the output fixes this. (a) Fundamental amplitude 1 (gain pi/4, as in the reference): max_abs 0.932. (b) Peak normalised to 1: rms 0.762, above the 0.7425 limit. (c) RMS normalised to 0.7071: max_abs 0.928. Only a deliberately chosen gain between the two targets, or stronger filtering than the instruction asks for, passes. Scratch files: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-08/a_cutoff3300.grc and d_cutoff3300_rms_norm.grc. Numeric sweep: <scratchpad>/rev08/probe.py.
findings.suggested_fix: Preferred: drop the max_abs check. RMS already pins the amplitude and band_fraction already pins harmonic content. I checked this on a scratch copy without max_abs: './gb tier-f gates' passes everything, and the mutation gate still has 10 valid mutants with kill rate 1.0 and no survivors, so max_abs kills no mutant on its own. Alternatives: widen max_abs rel_tol to about 0.10-0.12 so it is consistent with the 99 % bound; or keep it, state the tolerance in the instruction ('peak amplitude within 5 % of 1') and raise the stated harmonic requirement to e.g. 'at least 99.9 % of the output power below 2.4 kHz'. The reference has band_fraction 1.0000, and cutoff 3000 Hz with width 1200 Hz gives 0.9998, so the variants still pass.

findings.claim: The oracle does not check the stated core requirement, 'turn a square wave into a clean sine wave' by repairing the flowgraph. A 'repair' that deletes the square-wave source, Add Const, Low Pass Filter and Multiply Const, and wires a 1.2 kHz amplitude-1 sine Signal Source straight into the File Sink, passes all V6 checks. That answer skips locating the fault altogether, and a real user would not accept it, because the whole point of the graph is to shape the square wave.
findings.evidence: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-08/b_sine_shortcut.grc has 2 functional blocks: analog_sig_source_x with GR_SIN_WAVE, freq 1200, amp 1, feeding blocks_file_sink shaped_sine.dat. Ladder result: first_failed None, highest_passed V6. peak_freq 1200.0, mean -0.0, band_fraction 1.0, rms 0.707105, max_abs 1.0, all PASS. None of the 10 mutations covers replacing the source, so the mutation gate cannot catch this.
findings.suggested_fix: A behavioural check cannot tell a filtered square wave from a synthetic sine, so this cannot be fixed inside the current oracle. Record it in review.notes as a known, accepted limitation. If the harness later supports structural guards, add one that requires a GR_SQR_WAVE Signal Source to stay upstream of the File Sink. Otherwise, consider reporting structural partial credit next to V6 for this item so that whole-graph replacements are visible.

findings.claim: peak_freq and mean are labelled 'p2p' (pass-to-pass: 'prior behaviour is preserved', proposal §5.2 [46]). But the start graph fails at V3 and never produces output, so no behaviour was observed that could be preserved. All five checks are in effect fail-to-pass. Any f2p/p2p breakdown reported for this item would claim the repair 'preserved' behaviour that never held.
findings.evidence: './gb ladder start.grc --task task.json' gives first_failed V3 with errors 'Source - out(0): Port is not connected.' and 'Sink - in(0): Port is not connected.'; there is no V5/V6 output, and gates.json start_fails.v6_groups is null. build.py justifies the labels as 'properties established upstream of the broken link', which describes the configuration, not observed behaviour. The same convention appears in gbf-dev-04, gbf-test-09 and gbf-test-10 (all repair items whose start fails at V2/V3), so it is a project-wide labelling choice and not specific to this item.
findings.suggested_fix: For repair items whose start state fails before V5, either put every check in 'f2p', or have the team define p2p explicitly for this case (e.g. 'properties already set correctly in the start configuration') in the eval plan, so per-group reporting is not misread. This does not change pass/fail, which needs all groups.

compliance.verdict: The item mostly holds up under a compliance review. I re-ran './gb tier-f gates' and every gate passed, matching the author's report: solvability 10/10, size 335 tokens (limit 3000), all 3 variants reach V6, the start graph first fails at V3 as expected ('Port is not connected' on Source out(0) and Sink in(0)), and all 10 mutants reach V5 with every one killed. Split discipline is correct: signature_split of the reference chain returns 'test'. The id, directory and split agree. The licence, source, cluster_id, provenance, review, perturbation (false, as a composed chain should be) and fault (deleted_connection, V3) fields follow the spec. The canary appears only in task.json. Every mutation is spec-breaking, and every 'breaks' value names a spec property. Tolerances come from the instruction (frequency ±1%, amplitude ±5%, at least 99% of power below 2.4 kHz) and the analysis window is a whole number of periods. Alternative correct filters (width 100 Hz; cutoff 1800 Hz with width 600) and a filter-first ordering all pass. build.py regenerates every file byte-for-byte, both through its documented command and on repeat runs. Scratch work is in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-08 (regen/, cand/). Three findings remain. The main one (medium) is that the oracle cannot tell a repair from a replacement: a bare 1.2 kHz cosine source wired to shaped_sine.dat passes V1-V6, so the instruction's 'turn a square wave into a sine' requirement is never checked. The other two are low: the p2p labels are nominal, because the start graph never runs and so nothing passes in it; and the item uses the same repair template as training spec t04, although its graph differs and the stated disjointness rule is met. None of these makes the item wrong for answers that genuinely repair the flowgraph.

findings.claim: The oracle cannot tell a repair from a replacement. Any 1.2 kHz, unit-amplitude sine written to shaped_sine.dat passes V1-V6, so an answer that throws away the square-wave shaping chain the user asked to have repaired still counts as a successful repair. The p2p checks (peak_freq, mean) do not stop this, because a fresh sine source also satisfies them.
findings.evidence: I wrote two candidates in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-08/cand/ and ran './gb ladder <file> --task items/tier_f/test/gbf-test-08/task.json' on each. (a) a_pure_cosine.grc: a GR_COS_WAVE Signal Source (1200 Hz, amp 1) wired straight to the File Sink shaped_sine.dat. Result: highest V6, first_failed None (peak_freq 1200.0, mean 0.0, band_fraction 1.0, rms 0.707105, max_abs 1.0). (b) b_square_kept_but_bypassed.grc: the square source and Add Const are parked on a Null Sink and a separate sine source feeds the File Sink. Result: also passes every check. The instruction's core intent ('This flowgraph is supposed to turn a square wave into a clean sine wave ... Repair the flowgraph so that it produces this output') is in neither spec_properties nor the oracle. Eval plan §4.3 says repair tasks check that 'everything that worked in the starting flowgraph still works', and here nothing enforces that.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one: (1) add a p2p structural assertion, if the harness can be extended, that the path into shaped_sine.dat starts at an analog_sig_source_x with waveform GR_SQR_WAVE; (2) add a second observation point on the square source's output edge with a p2p check that it is still a 1.2 kHz square wave (band_fraction(0-2.4 kHz) about 0.81, mean about 1). This assumes the start graph's block names are kept, and the variants would need those names too; (3) at minimum, record in review.notes that a direct sine source is accepted, so the team decides knowingly. The same limitation probably affects the other composed repair items.

findings.claim: The p2p group is only nominal. The start graph fails at V3 and never reaches V6, so no check passes in the starting flowgraph. Labelling peak_freq and mean as pass-to-pass contradicts the project's own definition. The split between p2p and f2p is also arbitrary: the output mean depends on the Low Pass Filter's DC gain and on the Multiply Const, both downstream of the deleted link.
findings.evidence: gates.json from my re-run: start_fails.first_failed = 'V3', v6_groups = null. The build.py docstring says 'The start graph does not run, so every check fails there.' oracles.py docstring: p2p = 'behaviour that held in the starting flowgraph still holds'. Eval plan line 112: 'everything that worked in the starting flowgraph still works'. Other repair items whose start fails before V6 use the same convention (gbf-dev-04 V3, gbf-test-09 V3, gbf-test-10 V2), so this affects the whole set, not just this item.
findings.suggested_fix: For repair items whose start fails before V6, either label every check f2p (or 'main'), or have the team define p2p for pre-V6 faults explicitly (for example 'properties encoded by blocks the fault did not touch') in the eval plan, and note it in review.notes. That keeps any reported f2p/p2p breakdown from being misread as regression preservation.

findings.claim: The disjointness statement is accurate at the graph level, but the item uses the same repair template as training-side spec t04_broken_sink_repair: one deleted connection, the symptom 'GRC complains about unconnected ports when generating', and the fix 'add the single missing connection'. The instruction's symptom sentence closely paraphrases t04's goal text. This does not break the stated rule; I flag it so the reviewers can see the overlap.
findings.evidence: reports/reference/training_task_specs.json has t04: 'my graph keeps complaining about something unconnected when i generate it ... please fix it' (qoherent_collection_task plus two sft_quarantined_session entries). The t04 seed ~/grc-agent/tests/data/broken_unconnected_sink.grc is a 350 Hz Signal Source feeding a Throttle, with the Throttle output and the Audio Sink input unconnected, so the disjointness line's description of it is correct. The gbf-test-08 instruction says: 'At the moment GRC refuses to generate the flowgraph, because validation reports ports that are not connected.' The start graph has exactly the two unconnected ports, Source out(0) and Sink in(0), confirmed by './gb ladder start.grc'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a clause to the disjointness line saying the deleted-connection/unconnected-port fault template is shared with t04 by design (the fault types are common to training and test), while the graph, the behavioural spec and the observation point differ. Optionally reword the symptom so it does not echo t04's goal phrasing, for example by stating only that generation fails with validation errors.
